prompt: Edit image 1 to a moment about five seconds later in the same shot. The camera eases back about a quarter and slides to the right, keeping the dog at the left edge of the frame so the whole right half of the sheet is in view. Keep the table and its wood grain, the single white sheet of paper with its edges, the green grass zigzag exactly as long as it is in image 1 (it is not extended), the tan dog with its blue checked blanket draped over its back exactly as drawn in image 1, Maria's pink sleeves, her two small hands, the green crayon and the warm low light exactly as in image 1; only her hands, sleeves and the crayon are in frame, no face. Change the page like this: where the faint grey pencil arc was, to the right of the dog and standing on the green grass line, MACA is now drawn in crayon, exactly as MACA is drawn in image 2: standing upright on the grass line with the head at the top, a round white head with a teal visor band across its face and two small round blue eyes, square shoulders, a pink rectangular chest panel with a neat row of five little round chest lights in red, yellow, green, blue and purple, white arms and legs with orange joints, feet on the grass, about three times as tall as the dog. Maria's right hand holds the green crayon low on the page and its tip touches the middle of MACA's pink chest panel, resting on the green chest light, the third of the five lights, which she is colouring now; the red and yellow lights to its left are already coloured, the blue and purple lights to its right are still empty outlines waiting to be coloured. The crayon tip is on the chest light, never on MACA's head, visor or shoulders. Image 2 is a flat crop of the finished family drawing, paper only, used only for how MACA is drawn and for the crayon style: take nothing else from it, not its framing and not its girl, and the dog, the grass, the sheet's edges and the table stay as image 1 shows them. MACA is never upside down and never lying on her side. The drawing is a child's crayon drawing on paper, crayon strokes and flat colour like the dog in image 1, with no grey pencil lines left on the page. Image 1 is the authority for render style, lens, lighting, room, furniture and colour: keep its finished 3D animated film look exactly, as if this were another frame of the same shot. Image 3 is the identity board, used only to confirm Maria's pink sleeve colour and MACA's design; never copy its painted style, its plain background or its poses; no figure from it appears in this frame. One instance of each drawn character only. Output one 16:9 full-colour production frame, 1280x720, no text, no sketch lines.
